div.div:
نَاضِحٌ (tropical:) A camel (S) or an ass or a bull (TA) upon which water is drawn (يَسْتَقَى عَلَيْهِ) [from a well &c.]: (S, TA:) a camel that carries water (يَحْمِلُ المَآءَ) from a river or canal or well to irrigate seed-produce; so called because it is a means of moistening [or allaying] thirst by the water which it carries: (Msb:) the female is called نَاضِحَةٌ (S, Msb) and سَانِيَةٌ [q. v.]: (S:) pl. نَوَاضِحُ. (Msb.) ―
-b2- Afterwards applied to Any camel: as in the following instance, occurring in a trad., أَطْعِمْهُ نَاضِحَكَ Give him thy camel to eat. (Msb.) ―
-b3- See نَضْحٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
